pr.title: Remove redundant union check in `KnownPanicsLint` const prop
pr.description:
Removes the below check which prevents unions from being const propagated:https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/f9dca46218d4b8efa062aec4fd0820cbb4942aa2/compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/known_panics_lint.rs#L587-L594

It is not needed because after PR #124504 we mark unions as `NoPropagation` over here: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/f9dca46218d4b8efa062aec4fd0820cbb4942aa2/compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/known_panics_lint.rs#L899-L902 which is enough to prevent them from being const propagated.
pr.author: gurry

analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically unsafe direction is to allow const propagation of union aggregate values, i.e. removing/eviscerating both union safeguards so a union local can be propagated and its fields evaluated as an `Aggregate` value. That yields propagated values that do not match the union's underlying layout type (the ICE #121534 failure mode). The merged patch removes only the `Aggregate` early-return and is safe solely because the `CanConstProp::check()` `NoPropagation` marking for `ty.is_union()` remains. Deleting the `Aggregate` guard without that marking (or weakening the marking) is the incorrect transformation to test against.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies processed by the `KnownPanicsLint` const propagator that contain union-typed locals and/or `AggregateKind::Adt` aggregates whose optional final (union discriminant) argument is `Some(_)`. This includes reads/writes of union fields and aggregate construction for union ADTs, where Rust "has no concept of an active variant of a union".
analysis.originalLogic: Before the patch, union handling was defended twice. In `ConstPropagator::eval_operand`'s `Aggregate` arm the code stated: "Do not const prop union fields as they can be made to produce values that don't match their underlying layout's type (see ICE #121534). If the last element of the `Adt` tuple is `Some` it indicates the ADT is a union", followed by `if let AggregateKind::Adt(_, _, _, _, Some(_)) = **kind { return None; };`. Separately, in `CanConstProp::check()`, every union-typed local is forced to `*val = ConstPropMode::NoPropagation;` with the comment that unions "can ICE during layout calc".
pitfalls: Do not treat the `Aggregate` union early-return as independently required: after PR #124504 it is redundant because union locals are already `NoPropagation`.

Conversely, do not delete the `NoPropagation` marking for `ty.is_union()`: it is the actual safeguard; without it unions could be const propagated and produce values inconsistent with their layout (ICE #121534).
Union const propagation is not a normal aggregate case: unlike enums/tuples, Rust has no active-variant concept for unions.

A retained/edited comment or test name alone does not demonstrate that a replacement pass is correct; verify which mechanism (`NoPropagation` marking vs. `Aggregate` early return) actually blocks propagation.
preconditions: The body is run through `KnownPanicsLint`'s const propagator (`ConstPropagator` / `CanConstProp`).
A union type is involved, either as a local type (`ty.is_union()`) or as an `AggregateKind::Adt` with the final tuple element `Some(_)`.
The `NoPropagation` marking in `CanConstProp::check()` is present and covers all union locals; this is what makes omitting the `Aggregate` guard safe.
analysis.summary: In `KnownPanicsLint` const propagation, union aggregate values must never be const-propagated. Historically two union guards existed: an `Aggregate`/`AggregateKind::Adt(.., Some(_))` early return in `ConstPropagator::eval_operand`, and a `ty.is_union()` -> `ConstPropMode::NoPropagation` marking in `CanConstProp::check()`. After the latter was introduced, the former became redundant. The reusable invariant is that the `NoPropagation` marking of every union-typed local is the load-bearing safeguard; the `Aggregate` guard can only be deleted while that marking remains.
analysis.testStrategy: Write a focused Rust UI test whose MIR exercises a union local (e.g. a union field written then read) plus a union aggregate construction, run through `KnownPanicsLint` const prop. Assert compilation succeeds with no layout-calc ICE and that the union local is not propagated. Construct two otherwise identical inputs to differentiate the guard variants: one where `CanConstProp::check()` marks union locals `NoPropagation` (expected: accepted, no ICE, no union propagation) and one where that marking is absent while only the redundant `Aggregate` guard is removed (expected: the unsafe configuration that can ICE or propagate layout-mismatched union values). Prefer MIR/UI checks over runtime behavior, since the invariant is a compile-time propagation restriction.
analysis.trigger: Const propagation reaching an `Aggregate` whose `AggregateKind` is a union ADT (`AggregateKind::Adt(_, _, _, _, Some(_))`), or any use of a union-typed local that `CanConstProp::check()` could otherwise mark as propagatable.
